title: Borrow upstream pdf-extract robustness patches
description: Track surgical upstream ports from jrmuizel/pdf-extract that materially improve extraction robustness, large-document performance, and malformed-font handling without regressing our chunking/citation pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: A prioritized set of upstream commits is tracked as child beads with explicit validation criteria against founder regression, fixed packs, and vendored parity.

title: Port upstream font-cache optimization (205c16f)
description: Port upstream commit 205c16f (Avoid reparsing fonts for every page). This is the highest-ROI upstream performance change for large PDFs and should reduce repeated font work on long docs like Puttaswamy.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical crate reuses parsed font objects across pages without changing extraction output semantics; founder regression remains green; large-document runtime is measurably improved on Puttaswamy or an equivalent long-doc fixture; vendored parity is synced.
notes: Already covered in fork: Processor now caches parsed fonts across pages via font_table; remaining work is perf verification.

title: Port upstream Type1C embedded encoding extraction (2ea7718)
description: Port upstream commit 2ea7718 (Extract encodings from embeded type1c fonts) using cff-parser to recover usable encoding data from embedded Type1C fonts. This is the strongest upstream candidate for generic glyph-soup reduction.
acceptance_criteria: Embedded Type1C font encodings are parsed and merged into decode flow; regression fixtures still pass; at least one known glyph-soup or malformed-font document shows reduced garbage output without a downstream cleanup hack; vendored parity is synced.
notes: Wave 1 landed: embedded Type1C encoding extraction added via cff-parser with ToUnicode precedence and soft-fail parse behavior.

title: Port upstream missing Widths fallback (701728c)
description: Port upstream commit 701728c (Handle missing Widths by substituting a font). This is a robustness patch for malformed PDFs that omit Widths and currently risk bad behavior or crashes.
acceptance_criteria: Fonts missing Widths no longer panic or catastrophically fail extraction; add or retain a fixture proving graceful degradation; no founder regression breakage; vendored parity is synced.
notes: Wave 1 landed: missing Widths now falls back to Helvetica metrics instead of panicking.

title: Port upstream Identity-V support (9395f7f)
description: Port upstream commit 9395f7f (Add support for Identity-V encoding). Cheap patch, low risk, likely useful for vertical/CID encoded PDFs and parity with LAParams detect_vertical behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Identity-V encoded PDFs decode without panic; add a focused regression fixture or test if possible; existing founder and fixed-pack regressions remain green; vendored parity is synced.
notes: Wave 1 landed: Identity-V accepted in ToUnicode/Encoding paths.

title: Port upstream Type3 unicode fallback (cf3866c)
description: Port upstream commit cf3866c (Handling missing unicode map entries in type 3 fonts better). Our PdfSimpleFont path already has fallback behavior, but PdfType3Font still has a gap.
acceptance_criteria: PdfType3Font falls back sanely when ToUnicode is incomplete and encoding data exists; add a focused test for missing Type3 unicode entries; no regressions on founder pack; vendored parity is synced.
notes: Wave 1 landed: PdfType3Font now falls back to encoding when unicode map entries are missing.

title: Port upstream DeviceN colorspace panic guard (4789858)
description: Port upstream commit 4789858 (Don't panic on DeviceN colorspaces). Not a founder-specific fix, but it hardens the extractor on weird PDFs.
acceptance_criteria: DeviceN colorspaces no longer panic extraction; if no fixture exists, add a targeted unit or fixture-backed test; no regression failures; vendored parity is synced.
notes: Wave 2 in progress: DeviceN colorspace no longer panics in make_colorspace.

title: Port upstream overflow panic guard (0f5955b)
description: Port upstream commit 0f5955b (Avoid indexing panics if we overflow). Small defensive fix; worth taking if the patch is still applicable.
acceptance_criteria: The identified indexing/overflow path is guarded in our fork, covered by a test where practical, and does not regress founder/fixed-pack results; vendored parity is synced.

title: PDFium/LiteParse parity and layout correctness
description: Track work from the PDFium/LiteParse review: fix local layout extraction inflation/corruption, preserve existing chunking and citation schema, and evaluate an optional PDFium raw backend for the Tauri desktop package.
acceptance_criteria: The review in docs/PDFIUM_LAYOUT_REVIEW.md is implemented through child tasks; small-document layout parity is gated; single-page PDFs no longer extract as zero; any PDFium integration preserves ContentCore/ContentExt, PdfLocation fragments, hard token caps, and no-system-dependency desktop packaging.

title: Add stage-level PDF extraction benchmark harness
description: Create a durable benchmark that compares pdftotext, LiteParse raw PDFium extraction, LiteParse parse projection, our no-layout path, and our layout/all_texts path on hello, documents_stack.pdf, 4.pdf, 10.pdf, and founder fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark command is checked in; outputs normalized chars, words, chunks, fragments, max chunk tokens, over-cap count, runtime, and text heads; artifacts land under eval/runs; docs explain how to rerun; the harness can run with OCR disabled and does not require system Tesseract.

title: Fix single-page header/footer false positives
description: HeaderFooterDetector currently treats every unique segment on a one-page PDF as repeated boilerplate because occurrence_ratio is occurrence_count / page_count and ratio 1.0 passes the 0.8 threshold. This deletes valid one-page PDFs such as hello and documents_stack.pdf.
acceptance_criteria: Repetition-based header/footer filtering is disabled for page_count < 3; two-page docs only remove strict page-number/header/footer regex matches; distinct pages, not occurrence count, drive ratios; tests cover one-page hello and documents_stack-like fixtures; PDF_EXTRACT_SKIP_HEADER_FOOTER is no longer needed for those fixtures.

title: Align layout visibility filtering with no-layout
description: The layout path accepts render modes 0, 1, and 2 directly, while no-layout uses is_visible_text with transform, color, media-box, and render-mode checks. Layout mode should not admit more hidden or decorative text than no-layout.
acceptance_criteria: Layout glyph admission calls the same visibility predicate as no-layout, with an explicit policy for invisible OCR-only pages; fixtures cover invisible text, white/off-page text, clipped text, and normal visible text; normalized char counts on 4.pdf and 10.pdf move toward no-layout/PDFium raw without losing visible content.

title: Instrument layout duplication by stage
description: Add diagnostics that report per-page glyph/segment/text counts before and after native page text, Form XObject recursion, vertical detection, table formatting, and header/footer filtering.
acceptance_criteria: A debug flag or env var emits structured per-page counters; the counters include chars, normalized chars, glyphs, segments, duplicate overlap counts, and stage labels; benchmark artifacts capture these diagnostics for 4.pdf, 10.pdf, hello, and documents_stack.pdf; normal output remains unchanged when diagnostics are disabled.

title: Deduplicate and correctly transform Form XObject text
description: all_texts=true recursively extracts Form XObject text, but the parent CTM path is suspicious and there is no strong dedup/gating policy. This is likely a major source of layout inflation and scrambled text.
acceptance_criteria: Recursive stream processing receives an explicit parent/initial CTM; Form XObject Matrix composition is covered by focused tests; text from forms is deduplicated by normalized content plus bbox overlap; form text can be gated when native page text is already sufficient; legal Form XObject fixtures keep needed text without 2x inflation.

title: Make vertical text detection non-duplicating
description: detect_vertical currently derives vertical lines from the same glyph set and appends them to normal lines using a height > 1.5 * width heuristic, which can duplicate ordinary Latin text.
acceptance_criteria: Vertical extraction requires angle/writing-mode evidence or a stronger fixture-backed heuristic; emitted vertical lines do not overlap equivalent horizontal lines; default examples/regression config does not enable detect_vertical blindly for Latin/legal fixtures; add tests for ordinary Latin text and at least one true vertical/CID case if available.

title: Add small-document layout parity gates
description: Turn the stage benchmark findings into regression gates so layout cannot drift far from Poppler/PDFium/no-layout text volume on simple documents.
acceptance_criteria: Tests or CI benchmark gates assert hello is nonzero and correct; documents_stack.pdf is nonzero; 4.pdf and 10.pdf layout normalized chars are within an agreed threshold of no-layout/PDFium raw; hard token caps remain enforced; failures print enough counters to identify the responsible stage.

title: Prototype optional PDFium raw extraction backend
description: Build a feature-gated backend that uses PDFium/LiteParse-style raw character extraction and maps it into our TextSegment model before existing post-processing and ChunkAccumulator logic.
acceptance_criteria: Backend returns TextSegment values with page, bbox, char ranges, font-ish metadata where available, and visible/invisible/generated character policy documented; output_doc_new_schema can use the backend without changing ContentCore/ContentExt; chunk IDs, hard caps, and PdfLocation fragments remain valid; benchmark compares backend against lopdf no-layout and layout paths.

title: Package PDFium backend for Tauri desktop
description: Define and verify packaging for a local Tauri desktop installer that vendors PDFium and avoids extra system dependencies. OCR/Tesseract must remain optional and disabled unless deliberately shipped.
acceptance_criteria: macOS, Windows, and Linux packaging plans specify where libpdfium.dylib/dll/so lives and how it is loaded; no system PDFium or Tesseract install is required; default build disables LiteParse/Tesseract default feature if used; licenses/notices are documented; smoke tests prove the app can extract a sample PDF from a clean desktop environment.

title: Document safe layout defaults and integration guidance
description: Update docs and examples so downstream users do not blindly enable all_texts=true and detect_vertical=true without understanding their correctness and duplication risks.
acceptance_criteria: ARCHITECTURE/INTEGRATION/example docs explain when to use no-layout, layout, all_texts, detect_vertical, and future PDFium backend; examples use safe defaults; docs state that LiteParse parse projection mutates coordinates and is not citation-safe; vendored parity docs mention the new gates.
